question_text: Find the number of ways of arranging the letters of the word INTERMEDIATE.

mark_split.label: Count the letters and the repeats

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the arrangements of the word INTERMEDIATE — what you count first and which formula you use.
insider_note: INTERMEDIATE has three repeat groups, not two: E three times, and both I and T twice. The middle E and the second pair are the usual misses — write the word out and number its 12 letters before applying the formula.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the letters and the repeats
steps.margin_note: First mark. I-N-T-E-R-M-E-D-I-A-T-E: 12 letters. E appears 3 times, I twice, T twice; the rest once.
steps.memory_tip: Write it out: I-N-T-E-R-M-E-D-I-A-T-E. Three repeat groups — E three times, I twice, T twice.
lines: E three times, I twice, T twice.

recall.must_convey: That INTERMEDIATE has 12 letters with E three times, I twice and T twice.
accept: twelve letters, E three times, I twice, T twice
count the letters, twelve, with three E, two I and two T
the word has twelve letters and the repeats are E three, I two, T two
twelve letters, E moodu sarlu, I rendu, T rendu
find the repeated letters first, E I and T

steps.why: Alike letters cannot be told apart, so swapping them does not give a new arrangement. The count of each repeated letter is what the formula divides by, so it must be found before anything else.
common_mistakes: Counting E twice instead of three times (the E in the middle is easy to miss).
Counting 11 letters — write the word out and number them.

steps.label: Apply n!/(p!·q!·r!)
steps.memory_tip: 12!/(3!·2!·2!) = 1,99,58,400. The divisor is a product of factorials, not (3+2+2)!.

recall.must_convey: That the count is 12 factorial over 3 factorial times 2 factorial times 2 factorial.
accept: twelve factorial over three factorial two factorial two factorial
n factorial by p factorial q factorial r factorial, twelve factorial by three factorial two factorial two factorial
divide twelve factorial by twenty four
twelve factorial by three factorial into two factorial into two factorial
the answer is twelve factorial over three factorial two factorial two factorial which is about two crore

steps.why: n! counts the arrangements as if every letter were different; each group of p alike letters has been counted p! times over, so dividing by p! for each group leaves the true count.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 3!·2! only and forgetting the second repeated pair.
